security_spec.violation_condition: The XiangShan FPU execute pipeline takes data-dependent cycle counts when processing fdiv.s, fmul.s, fmadd.s, fmsub.s, fnmadd.s, or fnmsub.s instructions. Specifically: (a) subnormal operands trigger the softfloat_normSubnormalF32Sig normalization path which may take extra microarchitectural cycles vs normal operands; (b) NaN operands (exp==0xFF with nonzero sig) take the softfloat_propagateNaNF32UI fast-return path, creating a timing differential vs normal computation; (c) zero operands take early-return paths with different latency; (d) the fused multiply-add sign/subtraction case where both operands are equal and opposite-sign zeros (returning +0 or -0 depending on RDN mode) is a rarely-triggered microarchitectural corner case with potentially unique timing. The spec declares data_independent_timing: true for all these instructions, meaning any cycle-count variation based on operand class violates the spec and constitutes an observable timing side channel.
security_spec.summary: Six single-precision FP instructions newly declare data_independent_timing: true; any operand-value-dependent execution latency in the XiangShan FPU pipeline (subnormal normalization, NaN fast-return, zero bypass) is a timing side-channel violation
